run.question: We're getting mapping errors and slow indexing on our events index. Can you check the field mappings for our app-188-index-* indexes and tell me if any have an unusually high number of fields? What's the exact field count for each?

report.summary: Mappings were read for all four indices matching app-188-index-* (app-188-index-a, -b, -c, -x; these four are also the only indices the cluster reports at query time). Exact field counts: app-188-index-a = 10 top-level mapped fields (10 field definitions, no multi-fields, no nested sub-fields); app-188-index-b = 10 (10); app-188-index-c = 10 (10); app-188-index-x = 523 top-level mapped fields and 655 field definitions once its 132 keyword multi-fields are counted. app-188-index-x is therefore the clear outlier: 52x the field count of its siblings, made up of 130 counter_* (long), 130 flag_* (boolean), 130 label_* (text + keyword) and 130 metric_* (long/float) generated fields plus @timestamp, event_type (text + keyword) and user_id (text + keyword). The one document present in app-188-index-x carries that same generated field family (~520 generated keys in one _source), so the field growth is driven by document shape, not by unused leftover mappings. The three sibling indices carry a different, small event schema (including metadata as type object). What is NOT established: the reported mapping errors and slow indexing. No Elasticsearch server log or error-message source exists in this environment (only these 4 indices exist; there is no logs-* index), index settings such as index.mapping.total_fields.limit / dynamic / dynamic_templates are not readable with the available tools, and index_time_in_millis (6 ms cumulative for app-188-index-x) has no comparable baseline, so neither the error text nor the latency claim can be confirmed or refuted. Cluster health for all four indices is green with 0 unassigned shards and no pending tasks, and each index reports index_failed = 0 (cumulative since index creation), which is counter-evidence against currently-recorded rejected writes but cannot rule out past failures if these indices were recreated.

claims.text: Four indices match app-188-index-*: app-188-index-a, app-188-index-b, app-188-index-c and app-188-index-x; all are open with health green, and doc counts are 0, 0, 0 and 1 respectively (app-188-index-x store size 198.3kb vs 227b for the others). All four were returned by the list of all indices (pattern *), i.e. the cluster reported no other indices.

Exact field counts from the mappings: app-188-index-a = 10 top-level fields / 10 total field definitions; app-188-index-b = 10 / 10; app-188-index-c = 10 / 10; app-188-index-x = 523 top-level fields / 655 total field definitions (523 top-level + 132 multi-field sub-fields). None of a, b, c has object sub-fields or multi-fields.

app-188-index-x's 523 top-level fields are: 1 @timestamp (date), 130 counter_* (long), 130 flag_* (boolean), 130 label_* (text), 130 metric_* (mixed dynamic types, long and float), plus event_type and user_id (both text). Fields outside the counter_/flag_/label_/metric_ families are only @timestamp, event_type and user_id.

The 132 multi-fields in app-188-index-x are keyword sub-fields (ignore_above 256) on event_type, user_id and the 130 label_* fields; counter_* and flag_* carry no multi-fields. event_type and user_id are mapped text with a keyword sub-field, and metric_* entries are numeric (e.g. metric_0000 long, metric_0004 float).

app-188-index-a, -b and -c share an identical 10-field schema: @timestamp date, action keyword, duration_ms integer, error_message text, event_type keyword, ip_address ip, metadata object (no sub-fields mapped), session_id (type value returned redacted by the tool), status keyword, user_id keyword. This differs from app-188-index-x, which has no action/duration_ms/error_message/ip_address/metadata/status/session_id fields and maps event_type/user_id as text rather than keyword.

The single document stored in app-188-index-x (@timestamp 2026-11-23T17:41:00Z) contains the whole generated field family in one document: counter_0001 through counter_0517, flag_0002 through flag_0518, label_0003 through label_0519, metric_0000 through metric_0516, plus @timestamp, event_type (user_action) and user_id. The per-document field count therefore matches the mapping's generated families rather than a small set of used fields.

Cumulative index counters: app-188-index-x has indexing.index_total 2, docs.deleted 1, index_failed 0, index_time_in_millis 6; app-188-index-a, -b and -c each have index_total 0, docs.count 0, index_failed 0, index_time_in_millis 0. These counters are cumulative since index creation, not window-scoped.

Cluster health for app-188-index-* is green: cluster status green, 1 node / 1 data node, each index 1 shard with 0 replicas, 0 unassigned shards, 0 initializing/relocating shards, 0 pending tasks, task_max_waiting_in_queue_millis 0.

app-188-index-x's oversized mapping (523 top-level / 655 total field definitions, ~520 generated fields per document) is a plausible contributor to both reported symptoms: every indexing request must resolve and carry hundreds of generated fields, and each mapping update forces cluster-state propagation, so per-document cost and mapping-merge work grow with the field count. This is a hypothesis because no error text, index settings or latency baseline were observable to tie it to the reported mapping errors or slow indexing.

A second candidate mechanism for the mapping errors is a dynamic type conflict on the generated families in app-188-index-x: metric_* fields are mapped with mixed inferred types (long and float appear among metric_*), so a document supplying a value that cannot be coerced to the type already inferred for a given metric_NNN (for example a decimal or string for a long-mapped counter_*), or a document changing the shape of a field, would be rejected with a parse/mapping exception. No such error text was observed, so this remains unverified.

A third candidate, specific to the three small indices, is a type mismatch against their fixed 10-field schema (for example a document sending metadata as a non-object although metadata is mapped object with no sub-fields, or sending event_type/user_id as text where the index maps keyword). No documents exist in app-188-index-a/-b/-c (docs.count 0) and no error text was available, so this cannot be confirmed or excluded.

No failed indexing operations are currently recorded: index_failed is 0 for all four indices and index_failed_due_to_version_conflict is 0, with is_throttled false and throttle_time_in_millis 0 on each. This argues against rejected document writes in the current instances of these indices, but the counters are cumulative since index creation and reset if an index is recreated, so they cannot rule out earlier mapping errors.

The cluster is not in a degraded allocation or queue state: health green, 0 unassigned/initializing/relocating shards, 0 pending tasks, task_max_waiting_in_queue_millis 0, so the oversized mapping has not produced observable shard-allocation or task-queue pressure at query time.

Rejected: that the high field count is shared across all app-188-index-* indices. The mappings show 10 top-level fields (10 field definitions) for app-188-index-a, -b and -c versus 523 top-level fields (655 field definitions) for app-188-index-x; only app-188-index-x is the outlier.

Read app-188-index-x's index settings (index.mapping.total_fields.limit, index.mapping.dynamic, dynamic_templates) and its index template, since these are not readable with the tools available here; a 655-field definition count is far above the 10 of its siblings and is the figure to compare against the configured total-fields limit.

Capture the exact mapper_parsing_exception / illegal_argument_exception text from the indexing client and the Elasticsearch server log for app-188-index-x; that message names the field and the mapped type, which would confirm or eliminate the dynamic type-conflict hypothesis, and it is the missing evidence for the reported mapping errors.

Reduce app-188-index-x's per-document field cardinality at the writer (the generated counter_NNNN/flag_NNNN/label_NNNN/metric_NNNN naming is what produces ~520 fields per document); mapping the families as flattened or disabling dynamic mapping for them would stop further field growth, and index_time_in_millis should then be compared against a pre-change baseline, which does not exist today.

gaps: No Elasticsearch server log or error-message data source was available: the cluster reports only the four app-188-index-* indices (no logs-* or .monitoring index), so the text of the reported mapping errors could not be read or verified.

Index settings that govern field growth and would explain mapping errors (index.mapping.total_fields.limit, index.mapping.dynamic, dynamic_templates) and any index template could not be read with the available tools.
The mapped type of session_id in app-188-index-a/-b/-c was returned redacted by the tool, so that field's type could not be verified.

'Slow indexing' is unverified: index_time_in_millis (6 ms total for app-188-index-x, 0 for the siblings) is a cumulative counter with no comparable baseline and no time series, so no latency trend can be established.

When the generated counter_/flag_/label_/metric_ fields were introduced, and whether app-188-index-x was ever recreated (which would reset the index_failed=0 evidence), cannot be determined from the tools used.
Change history is not integrated in this Run, so no change record could be checked against the mapping growth or the reported errors.
Whether documents are routed to app-188-index-a/-b/-c at all is unknown: all three reported docs.count 0, so their mappings' behaviour under real writes was not observed.
next_steps: Retrieve app-188-index-x's _settings and _template/_index_template definitions to confirm the total-fields limit, dynamic setting and any dynamic_templates driving the counter_/flag_/label_/metric_ fields.
Pull the indexing client's error responses and the Elasticsearch server log around the reported mapping errors to obtain the exact field name and mapped type in the exception.

Have the application team confirm whether the generated counter_NNNN/flag_NNNN/label_NNNN/metric_NNNN fields are intentional; if not, stop emitting them or map them as flattened to prevent further field growth toward the total-fields limit.

query.jq: to_entries[] | {index: .key, top_level_count: (.value.mappings.properties|keys|length), total_field_defs: ([.value.mappings | .. | objects | select(has("type"))] | length), object_fields: ([.value.mappings.properties | to_entries[] | select(.value.properties or .value.fields) | {name: .key, sub_fields: ((.value.properties//{})|keys|length), multi_fields: ((.value.fields//{})|keys|length)}])}

.[].mappings.properties | {base_fields: (to_entries | map(select(.key|test("^[a-z_]+$"))) | map({name:.key, type:.value.type, fields:(.value.fields//null)})), sample_generated: (to_entries | map(select(.key|test("^metric_"))) | .[0:2]), dynamic: null}
.[].mappings.properties | to_entries | group_by(.key|sub("_[0-9]+$";"")) | map({prefix: (.[0].key|sub("_[0-9]+$";"")), count: length, sample_types: ([.[].value.type]|unique)})

to_entries[] | {index: .key, field_count: (.value.mappings.properties|keys|length), fields: (.value.mappings.properties | to_entries | map({(.key): ((.value.type//"none") + (if .value.fields then "+[" + (.value.fields|keys|join(",")) + "]" else "" end))}) | add)}
